rubrics.justification: The response overcalls several image features and conflicts with the provided Gardner 3AB label, describing the embryo as less expanded with a relatively thick zona and uncertain ICM/TE; some observations are plausible, but the morphology assessment is not well matched to the stated grading and visible image.

It integrates age, diagnosis, ovarian reserve signal, semen quality, BMI, endometrium, and prior ectopic/miscarriage into prognosis reasonably well, though AMH is unavailable and some links are somewhat generic.

The reasoning is structured and mostly internally consistent, with conclusions generally following from embryo quality plus favorable patient factors; the main weakness is the morphology downgrade driving prognosis despite the supplied 3AB grade.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice guidelines: single-embryo transfer counseling, luteal support, ectopic surveillance, and hydrosalpinx consideration are appropriate. Minor issues include speculative emphasis on day-4 blastocyst timing and somewhat imprecise use of morphology terminology.

Provides practical next steps for transfer, follow-up, lifestyle modification, and future-cycle review, including hydrosalpinx assessment and early hCG/ultrasound monitoring; useful though not highly individualized beyond standard care.
